standard_prerequisites: The map J_n: the affine Grassmannian elements of type A_{n-1}^(1) to binary words, defined by the unnumbered display at source lines 3078-3083 (c_k = 1 iff k >= w(i)-1 with k = w(i)-1 mod n), immediately preceding the statement.
Lemma lem:indices (printed 18.2): the index correspondence between boxes of the core partition and congruence classes of the binary word.
Equation eq:ineg (printed (7.2)): the inequality system closing the count, established just before the statement.
The inversion set R(w) of an affine permutation and its height grading ht_n.
core_obligations: For w in the affine Grassmannian of type A_{n-1}^(1) and lambda = Psi^{-1}(J_n(w)) the corresponding n-core: for every i in {1,...,n-1}, the number of inversions alpha in R_i(w) (those with ht_n(w^{-1}(alpha)) = n-i) equals the number of hooks of lambda of length n-i.
proof_roadmap: Decompose an inversion alpha = eps_a - eps_b + k delta with the congruence w^{-1}(a) - w^{-1}(b) = n-i mod n; re-center a and b on the finite window via a = w(c) + m_a n, b = w(d) + m_b n.
Unfold the definition of J_n into the two explicit congruence classes of word positions (the align* display).

Invoke Lemma lem:indices to convert the word classes into the explicit set of boxes with hook length n-i, and close the count with the inequalities (7.2) via the reindexing k'' = k + m_a + indicator(a>b).
